test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 23 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting around a circular table, facing away from the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 2 people sit between A and D when counted from the right of D. B and C are both immediate neighbours of G. F sits to the immediate left of E. Only 1 person sits between C and E when counted from the left of C. How many people are sitting between G and D when counted from the right of G?
solution:
Given, A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting around a circular table, facing away from the centre (but not necessarily in the same order).

Only 1 person sits between C and E when counted from the left of C.

F sits to the immediate left of E.

B and C are both immediate neighbours of G.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfc25bceeaf6911f628740e4f4661c824a5d7536a426e5f295c40674bbb2d484.png] 

Only 2 people sit between A and D when counted from the right of D.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9914d1a935e3fcbc7d5d4e37e8b820df41767f9872fd4044b50c0a8947ea3
216.png] 

So, 1 people is sitting between G and D when counted from the right of G.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 4".**
